text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 3.4% today after crude oil prices rallied sharply over the past two days. US oil recovered to $99.64 per barrel (up from lows near $90 last week), driven by renewed uncertainty about Iran tensions despite Trump administration statements suggesting the conflict could end soon—mixed signals that are keeping energy markets volatile. Refineries are running at 94.5% capacity, near full utilization, which means refiners benefit when crude prices rise because they can convert it into higher-margin products like gasoline and diesel.

The stock's bounce today reverses a brutal eight-day slide (down 8.6% since early November) that hit hard as oil prices fell on hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough and reduced geopolitical risk. Today's move reflects crude's rebound, but the underlying uncertainty—diplomatic talks appear stalled despite administration optimism—suggests oil and refiner stocks could remain choppy until the geopolitical picture clears.
